bull_bear.body:
- Well placed to address unmet demand in a large and growing molecular diagnostic market with gaining credence of point-of-care testing - global POCT total addressable market of USD 29.3 billion (Rs 2,588.6 billion) projected to grow at 17.9% CAGR between 2025 and 2030 to USD 67.1 billion (Rs 5,928.2 billion) (Source: 1Lattice Report)
- Innovative, R&D focused business - R&D spend of Rs 874.56 million, Rs 685.69 million and Rs 597.77 million (6.05%, 6.72% and 7.15% of revenue from operations) in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; 16 patents, 29 trademarks, 11 designs and 3 copyrights registered in India and 191 patents in foreign jurisdictions
- Developed and commercialized a novel portable multi-disease POC molecular diagnostics platform - fully automated, battery-operated, room-temperature-stable kits, ~60 minute turnaround, 1/2/4 simultaneous samples, wireless connectivity and remote software updates
- Scalable closed-system business model with strong entry barriers and a high proportion of recurring revenues - Truenat devices work exclusively with Truenat test kits; test kit revenue was Rs 10,348.20 million, 73.98% of Fiscal 2026 finished-goods revenue
- Oligopolistic market with high entry barriers - the platform underwent 13 years of R&D to obtain ICMR certification, and the Truenat TB test chip is the only one by an Indian company and one of only two rapid molecular tests in the world endorsed by the WHO for initial diagnosis of TB and rifampicin resistance detection (Source: 1Lattice Report)
- Patent and regulatory moat - Truenat is patented in more than 100 countries as of March 31, 2026; quality systems certified under ISO 13485 and MDSAP covering CDSCO, EU, ANVISA, Health Canada and US FDA criteria
- Strategic collaborations and acquisitions enhancing capabilities and offerings - Prognosys (radiology, enabling end-to-end TB screening plus confirmatory testing) and OptraScan (digital pathology), plus development collaborations with Xcyton, Stellar, Testi, HealSeq, UE Lifesciences and Equine Biotech
- Management team with deep domain expertise and a track record of delivering strong financial performance - CEO Sriram Natarajan (35 years, co-founder of Tulip Diagnostics, exited to PerkinElmer in 2017) and CTO Dr. Chandrasekhar Bhaskaran Nair (34 years, Infosys Prize 2021)
- Installed manufacturing infrastructure built ahead of demand - installed capacity of 5,400 devices and 39,000,000 Truenat test kits per annum as of March 31, 2026, at Fiscal 2026 utilisation of 42.30% (devices) and 58.25% (test kits), described as prepared for future growth
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Government and international aid agency revenue concentration - 84.56%, 87.83% and 91.60% of revenue from contracts with customers - sale of products - finished goods in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 — Revenue depends on Indian Central and State government and aid agency public healthcare programs procured through competitive tenders; unfavourable policy changes or a decrease in funding for those programs would directly reduce product sales, and payment cycles from public health programs are long, lifting working capital needs
- Customer concentration - the top 10 customers were 83.26%, 83.62% and 78.54% of finished-goods revenue in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 — The loss of any of these customers or a decline in their demand would have an adverse effect on business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows; there is limited diversification to absorb the loss of a single large tender
- Single-disease product concentration - TB test kits were 70.20%, 69.11% and 62.40% of finished-goods revenue in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 — The economics rest on one disease programme; the intended expansion into an additional 34 assays for 22 diseases is unproven, so any shift in TB programme funding, protocol or competitive technology has an outsized effect
- Supplier concentration and import dependence - the top 10 suppliers were 58.52%, 58.21% and 58.52% of raw materials and components consumed in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, and imported raw material purchases were 42.01% of Fiscal 2026 purchases — No long-term supply contracts are in place (purchase orders are placed from time to time) for enzymes, primers, probes, electronic components and chips; import restrictions, embargoes or duty increases would hit margins, and raw material cost is already 46.66% of total expenses
- Working capital intensity and rising leverage — Working Capital Days of 166, 173 and 187 in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; working capital loans of Rs 1,801.94 million as of March 31, 2026; non-current borrowings rose from Rs 61.44 million (March 31, 2025) to Rs 2,124.06 million (March 31, 2026) and current borrowings from Rs 1,170.19 million to Rs 2,002.32 million, while total liabilities rose from Rs 4,942.70 million to Rs 8,396.48 million
- Low and volatile capacity utilisation across the manufacturing base — Fiscal 2026 utilisation was 42.30% for devices and 58.25% for test kits (Fiscal 2025: 58.89% and 43.44%; Fiscal 2024: 19.83% and 27.45%); the Prognosys X-ray line ran at 50.71% and the Pune digital pathology line at 27.50%, so fixed manufacturing costs are spread over well below installed capacity and further capex is proposed from the Net Proceeds
- Dependence on the Bigtec IP Agreement and a 10% of revenue royalty on a short remaining term — The core micro-PCR intellectual property sits with Subsidiary Bigtec and is licensed to the Company against royalty of 10% of revenue from operations (Fiscal 2026 royalty expense Rs 1,233.62 million) plus a security deposit of up to Rs 2,000.00 million; the 15-year term from August 1, 2011 was extended by only one year with effect from August 1, 2026 pursuant to an addendum dated July 25, 2026
- Tax and regulatory disputes plus auditor emphasis of matter and qualifications — Pending direct and indirect tax claims of Rs 507.81 million (11 cases) against the Company and Rs 191.79 million (7 cases) against Subsidiaries; contingent liabilities as at March 31, 2026 include bank guarantees of Rs 900.98 million, direct tax disputes of Rs 461.48 million and indirect tax disputes of Rs 322.37 million; the Statutory Auditors' reports for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 include an emphasis of matter paragraph, modifications and certain qualifications under the reporting on other legal and regulatory requirements

business.body: Molbio develops, manufactures and sells the 'Truenat' point-of-care PCR platform - the Trueprep universal nucleic acid extraction device and the Truelab real-time PCR analyzer (UnoDx, Duo and Quattro variants) - together with disease-specific, room-temperature-stable 'Truenat' test kits that work exclusively with the platform. As of March 31, 2026 it offered molecular testing for 30 diseases through 43 assays, had sold over 12,500 devices in over 90 countries, and derived revenue from the sale of devices and test kits of Rs 12,381.04 million in Fiscal 2026. Products are sold globally to public health programs, diagnostic laboratories, and private and public hospitals; through Subsidiaries Prognosys and OptraScan and collaboration partner UE Lifesciences it also supplies radiology, digital pathology and breast health screening devices.

business.body:

- **Truenat disease-specific test kits (43 assays for 30 diseases as of March 31, 2026):** Truenat MTB / MTB-Rif (tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance), Truenat COVID, Truenat Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C, Truenat HIV viral load, Truenat HPV, Truenat CT/NG (Chlamydia trachomatis / Neisseria gonorrhoeae), Truenat Nipah virus test chip
- **Radiology / digital imaging (Subsidiary Prognosys, brand 'ProRad'; digital health platform 'ProDigi'):** Ultraportable X-ray systems, Mobile digital X-ray systems, Floor-mounted and ceiling-suspended X-ray systems, C-arm systems, Veterinary diagnostic imaging products and veterinary software applications
- **Digital pathology (Subsidiary OptraScan):** OS 15 Scanner (scans 15 slides), OS Ultra Series (80, 160, 240, 320, 400 & 480), OS Lite (wirelessly-enabled), AI-powered analysis tools and telepathology services
- **Collaboration products:** Promilless saliva-based enzymatic alcohol test strips (Testi Technologies), UE Lifesciences iBreastExam (IBE) breast health screening device

outlook.body:
- Expand our geographical presence in India and across the globe - deepen deployment at public and private laboratories and hospitals, focus on enhancing exports to regions where we already have a presence such as Africa and Southeast Asia, and expand into other regions such as Latin America
- Register the 'Truenat' platform in several new countries and enter the US and EU markets
- Continue to expand our suite of diagnostic solutions for multiple diseases - intend to expand the suite of tests for an additional 34 assays for 22 diseases, alongside continued investment in R&D and expansion of the sales and marketing network, and capitalise on imaging-based technologies
- Develop new POC platforms for other communicable and non-communicable diseases using advanced multiplex PCR technologies, targeting immunochemistry, hematology, histopathology, antimicrobial resistance detection and biochemistry
- Grow through strategic acquisitions and alliances - evaluate inorganic opportunities that consolidate market position, achieve operating leverage, or strengthen and expand the product portfolio, applying selection criteria of management skills, operation scale, technological capability, valuation and cultural fit
- Establish a Center of Excellence at Bengaluru by Fiscal 2028 to help medtech innovators move medical device concepts from prototype to validated, scalable, commercially manufacturable products, in collaboration with Indian and international incubators including in Africa and South East Asia
- Continue to enhance the EDGE program (introduced February 2024) to identify, curate and collaborate with medical technology startups and SMEs, culminating in co-development, manufacturing or global sales partnerships
- Leverage Prognosys's e-clinic approach and expand its veterinary diagnostic imaging vertical into international markets by obtaining the necessary regulatory approvals
- Automate manufacturing processes to improve quality consistency, cost efficiency and scalability and to support regulatory compliance with US FDA, ISO and EU CE marking standards
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Two capital expenditure programmes are to be funded from the Net Proceeds of the Fresh Issue. First, a new owned research and development facility and Center of Excellence at New Municipal No. 43, PID No. 11-59-43, Ring Road Industrial Suburb II Stage, Yeshwanthpur, Bengaluru, on 43,490 square feet of land owned by the Company under an absolute sale deed dated August 7, 2023 and free from encumbrances; the proposed facility will have a total built-up area of approximately 150,000 square feet, significantly larger than the existing rented R&D Unit, with the intended ability to scale, adapt and consolidate all R&D functions under one roof, and will be operated by wholly-owned Subsidiary Bigtec together with connected office space for the Company, Subsidiaries and Associate. Total estimated cost is Rs 1,251.21 million (per the Koncepo Project Report), of which up to Rs 1,055.35 million will be funded from the Net Proceeds, nil deployed as on July 15, 2026, with Rs 264.74 million estimated for deployment in Fiscal 2027 and Rs 790.62 million in Fiscal 2028. Second, purchase of plant, machinery and other equipment to automate manufacturing at Goa Unit I, Goa Unit II and the Visakhapatnam Unit - automatic precision liquid micro-volume filling machines, screening machines, pick and place machines (to reduce coefficient of variation) and product assembly and packing machines (to reduce manpower reliance and manufacturing cost) - at a total estimated cost of Rs 808.05 million, of which up to Rs 722.81 million will come from the Net Proceeds, nil deployed as on July 15, 2026, entirely scheduled for deployment in Fiscal 2027. Existing manufacturing capacity is described as already built ahead of demand: installed capacity of 5,400 devices and 39,000,000 Truenat test kits per annum as of March 31, 2026 running at 42.30% (devices) and 58.25% (test kits) utilisation in Fiscal 2026, with the Visakhapatnam device line expanded from 3,600 to 5,400 units per annum and the Peenya Bengaluru component line from 15,000,000 to 22,500,000 units per annum during Fiscal 2026. EMS vendors are also used to assemble Truenat devices as and when required to meet demand.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Volume of products manufactured and sold - devices sold rose from 2,011 (Fiscal 2024) to 2,180 (Fiscal 2025) to 2,524 (Fiscal 2026), and test kits from 8.80 million to 12.24 million to 17.56 million; the closed-system design means the installed device base drives recurring test kit demand
- Relationships with customers and healthcare programs - Indian Central and State governments and international aid agencies contributed 84.56% of Fiscal 2026 finished-goods revenue, procured through competitive tenders under programs such as the National Tuberculosis Elimination Program, National Vector Borne Disease Control Program, National Viral Hepatitis Control Program and NACO; adverse programme changes or reduced healthcare spending would reduce sales
- Availability and cost of raw materials - cost of raw material and components consumed is the largest cost component at 46.66%, 52.99% and 48.63% of total expenses in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; key inputs are enzymes, primers, probes, electronic components and chips, purchased on spot purchase orders rather than long-term contracts, with imports at 42.01% of Fiscal 2026 raw material purchases
- Periods of disease outbreaks - testing volumes rise during outbreaks and pandemics while a significant portion of costs such as employee benefit expense is fixed, producing year-on-year fluctuations expected to continue
- Research and development - R&D is conducted through Bigtec under the IP Agreement, which requires royalty of 10% of revenue from operations (Fiscal 2026 royalty expense Rs 1,233.62 million); R&D spend was 6.05% of Fiscal 2026 revenue from operations and the cost of new technology, facility upgrades and retaining R&D personnel is significant
- Success of new tests on the device and integration of acquired entities - TB tests were 70.20%, 69.11% and 62.40% of finished-goods revenue in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, so the commercial success of the intended additional 34 assays for 22 diseases, and realisation of synergies from the Prognosys and OptraScan acquisitions, will shape future results
- Working capital cycle - reliance on public health programs lengthens payment cycles; Working Capital Days were 166, 173 and 187 and trade payables turnover 4.53, 4.74 and 5.47 in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, with working capital loans of Rs 1,801.94 million against sanctioned limits of Rs 3,613.00 million as of March 31, 2026
- Product mix between devices and consumables - device revenue fell to 14.53% of Fiscal 2026 finished-goods revenue from 20.63% and 22.65% in Fiscals 2025 and 2024, while test kits rose to 73.98% from 74.31% and 67.78%, and 'Others' (mainly Prognosys-manufactured devices) rose to 11.49% from 5.06% and 9.57%
- Geographic mix - revenue from customers outside India was 9.62% of Fiscal 2026 revenue from operations, down from 19.32% in Fiscal 2025 and up from 9.83% in Fiscal 2024

business_ops.seasonality: 'Our business is not seasonal or cyclical, however, our results of operations can fluctuate based on factors such as disease outbreaks, which are unpredictable and impact sales volumes. Sudden outbreaks of infectious diseases can lead to a surge in demand for diagnostic tests, while periods of low disease prevalence can result in decreased testing volumes. Historically, we experienced that a greater share of our sales was made in the second half of the fiscal year, as government tenders were issued more heavily during that period.' The MD&A adds: 'We have typically seen an increase in healthcare spending by the Government during the second half of a Fiscal. Since the number of purchase orders that our customers place with us may differ from quarter to quarter, our revenues, results of operations and cash flows have fluctuated in the past and we expect this trend to continue in the future.' Risk Factor 26 separately flags that the sales cycle and sales demand are variable, making the business difficult to forecast.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Vertically integrated closed-system model. The Truenat platform (Trueprep extraction device + Truelab analyzer) is a closed system designed to work exclusively with the Company's own disease-specific Truenat test kits, so every installed device generates recurring consumable demand; new tests can be added to the installed base through a remote software update. 'Our vertical integration strategy allows us to bring healthcare innovations to market rapidly by streamlining the process from R&D to production, sales, and marketing. Through this approach, we combine design expertise, regulatory capabilities, and production know-how.' Backward into technology and product creation: R&D is done in-house through wholly-owned Subsidiary Bigtec Private Limited (incorporated 2000, wholly-owned since 2015; Bengaluru unit recognised by DSIR); 13 years of R&D preceded ICMR certification; 16 patents, 29 trademarks, 11 designs and 3 copyrights registered in India and 191 patents in foreign jurisdictions, with 7 patents and 10 designs applied for in India and 15 patents abroad. R&D team of 153 permanent employees including 136 scientists as of March 31, 2026; R&D spend Rs 8,745.6 lakhs / Rs 6,856.9 lakhs / Rs 5,977.7 lakhs, being 6.05% / 6.72% / 7.15% of revenue from operations in FY26/FY25/FY24. Manufacturing is in-house across six owned-operation (leased-land) facilities covering devices, chips, cartridges and reagents, with EMS vendors used only to assemble Truenat devices as and when required to meet demand. Forward integration into the screening pathway via acquisitions: Prognosys (65.47%, March 2023) adds ultraportable X-ray screening ahead of the confirmatory molecular test, plus the ProDigi/Tele-Rad digital health layer and mobile healthcare units; OptraScan (19.68% November 2024 rising to 60.00% via a second tranche on November 1, 2025) adds digital pathology scanning and telepathology. Not integrated upstream into raw materials: principal inputs are substrates, primers and probes, enzymes, dNTP, electronic components and chemicals, procured on individual purchase orders with no long-term supply contracts; certain materials are imported from South Korea, Switzerland, Denmark and Singapore, substrates come exclusively from a single supplier, and the top 10 suppliers accounted for 58.52% / 58.21% / 58.52% of purchases of raw materials and components consumed. Cost of raw material and components consumed was 46.66% / 52.99% / 48.63% of total expenses in FY26/FY25/FY24. Third-party logistics providers handle road and sea transport (freight 1.51% / 1.74% / 1.35% of total expenses).

market_position.basis: The RHP states that 'There are no directly comparable listed companies in India or globally, that are of a comparable size and engage in a business similar to that of our Company.' Positioned as an innovative point-of-care ('POC') molecular diagnostics company built on the proprietary 'Truenat' micro-PCR platform - battery operated, usable in resource-limited settings, delivering decentralized results within 1 hour; molecular testing for 30 diseases as of March 31, 2026 (through 43 assays). The Company describes an oligopolistic market with high entry barriers, evidenced by 13 years of R&D to obtain ICMR certification; its 'Truenat' TB platform is the only one by an Indian company and one of only two rapid molecular tests in the world endorsed by the WHO for initial diagnosis of TB and rifampicin resistance detection (Source: 1Lattice Report). The 1Lattice Report states that for TB, hepatitis and HPV, HIV and STDs & STIs, two key players - Cepheid and Molbio - hold the major market share, and that Truenat has the highest market share in installations under India's NTEP (outside of Designated Microscopy Centres) from 2020 to 2022, holding a 92% share of incremental installations since 2019. No overall company market-share percentage is stated, so share_pct is null (the 92% figure is a narrow incremental-installation share, not a market share). For reference, the RHP's own industry peer group P/E block: highest 81.02, lowest 52.61, average 64.89, computed on the BSE closing price as on July 30, 2026 divided by diluted EPS for the fiscal ended March 31, 2026.

industry_peers.no_peer_note: MIXED DISCLOSURE - not silence. The RHP affirmatively states, under 'Industry peer group P/E ratio': 'There are no directly comparable listed companies in India or globally, that are of a comparable size and engage in a business similar to that of our Company.' It nonetheless provides a four-name peer table, stating twice (in the Basis for the Offer Price narrative and again below the table): 'Our Company has provided a comparison of its metrics referred to in this section with its nearest listed peer companies, i.e., Poly Medicure Limited, Dr. Lal Pathlabs Limited, Metropolis Limited and Vijaya Diagnostics Centre Limited. However, the business of our Company, in terms of key offerings, core business, business model and revenue type, varies considerably from that of the peers mentioned herein, and is accordingly not directly comparable with these peers. While we are an R&D, technology and IP-driven company involved in the manufacture of molecular diagnostics and point of care testing solutions, the listed peers mentioned herein are engaged either in the manufacture of disposable medical devices or in pathology diagnostic services. We are providing a comparison of our metrics referred to in this section with these companies only for reference as they are our nearest listed peers. However, we believe that we are unique in terms of our business and operations and are not directly comparable with the identified set of companies.' no_peer_flag is therefore false (a peer table exists and is populated), but the peer set is issuer-declared as non-comparable and must be treated as a reference set, not a valuation comparable set. The RHP separately notes that revenue from sale of devices and number of devices sold of Poly Medicure Limited are not directly comparable with those of the Company, and 'NA' is disclosed for those items elsewhere.

overview.business_model: The Company sells a closed-system diagnostics platform and the consumables that run on it. Revenue comes from selling the 'Truenat' platform hardware (Trueprep extraction devices and Truelab analyzers) and, on the installed base, disease-specific single-use 'Truenat' test kits that are designed to work exclusively with those devices and therefore generate recurring demand. As of March 31, 2026 it offers molecular testing for 30 diseases with 43 assays. The bulk of sales is to public buyers: revenue from Indian central/state governments and international aid agencies was 84.56%, 87.83% and 91.60% of revenue from contracts with customers - sale of products - finished goods in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, largely won through tendering under public health programmes (NTEP, NVBDCP, NVHCP, NACO). It also sells radiology, digital pathology and breast-health screening devices through its Subsidiaries Prognosys and OptraScan and collaboration partner UE Lifesciences.

CARO observations cover: delays in remittance of statutory dues (Company, Bigtec, Optrascan India, including dues outstanding more than six months); serious delays in a large number of cases at Bigtec including provident fund dues (FY25, FY24); fraud through misappropriation of earnest money deposits at Prognosys Medical Systems (FY24), fully provided for; misappropriation of funds by two external parties and by an employee of Bigtec; delays in repayment of a term loan and vehicle loans; non-physical-verification of property, plant and equipment, investment property and right-of-use assets (FY24) and PPE records maintained for groups of similar assets rather than individual assets (FY26, FY25, FY24).
financial_valuation.evidence: Misappropriation by two external parties ₹4.43 mn during Fiscal 2025 (two cyber complaints dated July 10, 2024 for ~₹2.02 mn and July 24, 2024 for ~₹2.41 mn); misappropriation by a Bigtec employee ₹6.09 mn in Fiscal 2024 arising from unauthorised payments for fake and inflated purchase orders amounting to ₹7.66 mn; employee dismissed and arrested. Loan repayment delays: FY2025 vehicle loan from Benz Financial Services India Private Limited ₹1.74 mn (1 day); FY2025 term loan from Tata Capital ₹28.13 mn (1 day); FY2024 vehicle loan from HDFC Bank ₹0.03 mn (15 days) - all subsequently paid. strategy_growth.detail: R&D is undertaken through the wholly-owned Subsidiary Bigtec Private Limited from a dedicated R&D unit in Bengaluru, Karnataka. As on the date of the Red Herring Prospectus the company intends to expand its suite of tests by an additional 34 assays for 22 diseases, covering both infectious and non-communicable diseases. Success depends on demonstrating accuracy and usability, obtaining regulatory clearances and approvals, and producing new tests in commercial quantities at acceptable cost. Marketing approval or clearance for new products or enhancements can take significant time, require substantial expense, involve rigorous pre-clinical and clinical testing and increased post-market surveillance, require product changes and result in limitations on indicated uses. The existing R&D unit is housed in a rented facility. The DRHP states no instance occurred in the last three Fiscals where a newly developed test or assay failed to receive regulatory approvals or was not commercialised.
strategy_growth.evidence: Assays developed and commercialised: 1 (FY26), 4 (FY25), 1 (FY24). Diseases for which tests were developed and commercialised: Nil (FY26), 4 (FY25 - Cytomegalovirus, Epstein-barr Virus, Leprosy, Mycoplasma genitalium infection), Nil (FY24). R&D spends ₹874.56 mn / 6.05% of revenue from operations (FY26), ₹685.69 mn / 6.72% (FY25), ₹597.77 mn / 7.15% (FY24) - all Bigtec expenses are treated as R&D expenses. R&D employees at Bigtec 153 (Mar 31, 2026), 114 (2025), 69 (2024). Up to ₹1,055.35 million of Net Proceeds proposed for the R&D facility, Center of Excellence and connected office space.

strategy_growth.detail: Net Proceeds are to fund (i) setting up of infrastructure for the R&D facility and Center of Excellence to be operated by Bigtec plus connected office space for the Company, Subsidiaries and Associate, and (ii) purchase of plant, machinery and other equipment for Goa Unit I, Goa Unit II and the Visakhapatnam Unit. No orders have been placed and no definitive agreements entered into; cost estimation relies on third-party quotations most of which are valid for a limited period and subject to revision, and on a detailed project report dated August 3, 2026 prepared by Koncepo Scientech International Private Limited for the R&D facility, Center of Excellence and connected office space, to be set up as a turnkey project. No payments or purchases have been made for any machinery/equipment. Cost variation factors include design or configuration changes, interest or exchange rate fluctuations and commodity prices including steel.

concerns_observed: Customer concentration is the central exposure and it is widening: the top-one customer was Rs 7,906.52 mn / 56.52% of finished-goods revenue in FY26, against 50.81% (FY25) and 33.83% (FY24); top five 73.83% and top ten 83.26%; government and international aid agencies together were 84.56% (FY26), 87.83% (FY25) and 91.60% (FY24). The RHP states there are no firm commitment agreements and business is conducted on purchase orders placed from time to time.

Single-disease dependence: TB test kits were Rs 9,820.12 mn / 70.20% of finished-goods revenue in FY26 (69.11% FY25, 62.40% FY24) and 96.02% of all kit units sold (16.86 mn of 17.56 mn); the next largest disease, Hepatitis B, was 1.33% of units.

The audit report on the FY2024 consolidated Ind AS financial statements carried a DISCLAIMER OF OPINION on internal financial controls under Section 143(3)(i) - the Holding Company 'has not established its internal financial control ... Accordingly, we do not express an opinion'; reports for FY2026 and FY2025 carried no disclaimer, but all three years carry Rule 11(g) audit-trail modifications, and FY2024 additionally carries a Rule 11(e) modification on funds advanced by the Group to an intermediary for further advancing to an ultimate beneficiary.

Cash conversion lagged profit sharply in FY26: cash flow from operating activities was Rs 503.85 mn against restated PBT of Rs 2,311.37 mn and restated PAT of Rs 1,641.40 mn, with trade receivables absorbing Rs (1,460.53) mn; trade receivables stood at Rs 4,087.36 mn at March 31, 2026 against Rs 2,716.60 mn a year earlier, and receivables outstanding beyond one year were Rs 5,790.3 lakhs, 5.06% of net worth.

Commission expenses rose to Rs 1,682.87 mn in FY26, 11.64% of revenue from operations, from Rs 648.53 mn / 6.36% (FY25) and Rs 389.86 mn / 4.66% (FY24) - the ratio more than doubled in one year while the share of revenue routed through distributors fell to 24.91% from 26.84% and 28.44%, and the distributor count was flat at 114 (115 in FY24).

Statutory-dues discipline: delays in remittance of undisputed statutory dues across FY24-FY26 with provident fund delayed 1 to 511 days, ESIC 1 to 770 days, professional taxes 1 to 236 days, TDS other than salaries 1 to 111 days; CARO for FY2026 records dues outstanding at year end for more than six months at two subsidiaries (Bigtec and Optrascan India), and CARO for FY2025/FY2024 records 'serious delays in a large number of cases' at Bigtec including provident fund dues.

A six-row compounding/adjudication table of past non-compliance under the Companies Act: penalties paid by the Company of Rs 32.00 mn under Section 135 (CSR for Fiscals 2022-2024, obligation Rs 140.67 mn), Rs 8.00 mn under Section 42(6) (private-placement moneys kept in existing bank accounts rather than a separate scheduled-bank account) and Rs 0.89 mn under Section 117(1); by Bigtec, Rs 28.29 mn under Section 135 and Rs 2.00 mn under Section 185 (loans to three group entities without the requisite shareholders' resolution, ratified only on March 4, 2025).

Income tax surveys under Section 133A were carried out at the Parent Company and Bigtec during the year ended March 2024 for AY 2020-21 to AY 2023-24 'on the ground that certain transactions classified as expenses in the books are bogus in nature'; demands aggregating Rs 234.17 mn plus interest and penalty were raised for AY 2020-21 to AY 2024-25, of which Rs 45.24 mn was paid as at March 31, 2026 and a further Rs 33.71 mn after year end, with appeals pending.

Three separate fraud/misappropriation matters are disclosed: earnest money deposits of Rs 199.00 mn misappropriated at subsidiary Prognosys Medical Systems (pre-acquisition, fully provided at March 31, 2024, Emphasis of Matter in the FY2024 report); Rs 6.09 mn by a Bigtec employee in FY2024 arising from unauthorised payments against fake and inflated purchase orders of Rs 7.66 mn; and Rs 4.43 mn by two external parties in FY2025. The Directorate of Enforcement issued a summons dated March 7, 2023 to a director of Prognosys Medical in the related West Bengal fake-tender matter, answered on March 20, 2023.

Execution risk on the Objects is front-loaded and unappraised: of the 18 plant-and-machinery line items only one order has been placed - Caliber LIMS, Rs 11.50 mn, purchase order dated March 30, 2026 - with the other 17 resting on vendor quotations dated June 20 to July 21, 2026; imported equipment is Rs 419.69 mn, stated as 51.94% of that object; the entire Rs 722.81 mn is scheduled for deployment in Fiscal 2027 with Nil deployed as on July 15, 2026; the R&D facility rests on a single Koncepo Scientech quotation dated July 26, 2026 valid to December 31, 2026, with handover scheduled March 2028; the fund requirements have not been appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency.

Leverage rose steeply in FY26: total debt Rs 41,263.8 lakhs at March 31, 2026 against Rs 12,316.3 lakhs a year earlier, with financing cash flow of Rs 2,760.66 mn driven by Rs 2,247.70 mn of long-term borrowing proceeds; total outstanding borrowings were Rs 4,225.01 mn as of May 31, 2026, of which Rs 392.43 mn of unsecured loans are repayable on demand, and the Company states it has not received any credit rating in the last three Fiscals.

Eighteen material licence applications to CDSCO and the Directorate of Food & Drugs Administration were applied for and not received as on the RHP date, including a Form MD-7 application (ref MFG/IVD/2022/55739) filed February 24, 2022 and a Form MD-24 clinical performance evaluation permission (ref CI/IVD/2022/61222) filed June 2, 2022 - both pending over four years.

Management and board continuity: three Chief Financial Officers since May 2023 (Suhas Ravindra Advant to March 26, 2024; Amol Narayan Lone June 5, 2024 to December 9, 2025; Manan Bimal Khokhani from December 22, 2025); all three nominee directors resigned in August 2025 (August 10 and August 13, 2025); only Dr. Balram Bhargava has prior listed-company board experience; the CEO sits on the Audit Committee; and the RHP states the Company does not have a business succession policy in place.

The Offer for Sale is up to 9,166,000 Equity Shares from 17 selling shareholders and those proceeds accrue to the sellers, not the Company; the weighted average cost of acquisition is Rs 0.20 per share for corporate Promoter Exxora Trading LLP and Rs 6.90 for Dr. Chandrasekhar Bhaskaran Nair, after a 4:1 bonus of 90,207,800 Equity Shares on July 29, 2025 that took paid-up capital from 22,551,950 to 112,759,750 shares within a year of the RHP.

The core micro-PCR licence is short-dated: the IP Agreement dated August 1, 2011 with wholly-owned Subsidiary Bigtec ran 15 years and was extended by only ONE year with effect from August 1, 2026 via an addendum dated July 25, 2026, with annual royalty during the extended term capped at up to 10% of topline revenue (royalty expense to Bigtec Rs 1,233.62 mn in FY26, Rs 929.59 mn FY25, Rs 739.28 mn FY24) and a security deposit of up to Rs 2,000.00 mn payable at regular intervals.

The peer set the RHP supplies is disclaimed by the issuer itself: the RHP states 'There are no directly comparable listed companies in India or globally, that are of a comparable size and engage in a business similar to that of our Company', then lists Poly Medicure, Dr. Lal Pathlabs, Metropolis and Vijaya Diagnostics as 'nearest listed peers' whose business 'varies considerably' - one disposable-device maker and three pathology-services chains that procure diagnostics rather than manufacture them; Cepheid, the only global player named as holding major share alongside Molbio, appears in no financial comparison table.

verdict.our_read: A Goa-based point-of-care molecular diagnostics maker (FY26 revenue Rs 14,456.87 mn, +41.68%; PAT Rs 1,641.40 mn; ROE 15.59%) whose earnings ride on one public-health demand pool: TB kits are 70.20% of finished-goods revenue and a single customer 56.52%.

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue from operations Rs 8,365.61 mn (FY24) to Rs 10,204.18 mn (FY25) to Rs 14,456.87 mn (FY26), the last step +41.68%; kit volumes 8.80 mn to 12.24 mn to 17.56 mn units; devices 2,011 to 2,180 to 2,524 units.

EBITDA margin 22.02% / 24.97% / 22.56% and PAT margin 9.94% / 13.48% / 11.28% across FY24-FY26 - FY26 growth of 41.68% came with margin compression on both lines; finance cost rose to Rs 3,346.6 lakhs from Rs 1,765.8 lakhs and commission expense to 11.64% of revenue from 6.36%.

FY26 CFO Rs 503.85 mn against restated PBT Rs 2,311.37 mn, with receivables absorbing Rs (1,460.53) mn; FY24 CFO was Rs 95.70 mn on PBT of Rs 1,296.39 mn; offset by working capital days improving 187 to 173 to 166 and the credit cycle shortening to 86 days from 125.

Net worth Rs 114,467.6 lakhs and cash Rs 35,553.0 lakhs at March 31, 2026 against total debt Rs 41,263.8 lakhs (Rs 12,316.3 lakhs a year earlier); borrowings Rs 4,225.01 mn at May 31, 2026 including Rs 392.43 mn repayable on demand; no promoter pledge; no credit rating obtained in the last three Fiscals.

Top-one customer 56.52% of finished-goods revenue (rising from 33.83% in FY24), top ten 83.26%; government and aid channels 84.56%; TB kits 70.20% of finished-goods revenue and 96.02% of kit units; no firm commitment agreements, purchase-order basis, tender-driven pricing with stated risk of price caps and procurement ceilings.

FY2024 disclaimer of opinion on internal financial controls; Rule 11(g) audit-trail modifications in all three years and a FY2024 Rule 11(e) modification on funds advanced to an intermediary; Form 1, Form 18 and Form 32 for incorporation and the CEO's first appointment untraceable at the Company and on the MCA Portal; three CFOs since May 2023; CEO on the Audit Committee; no business succession policy.

Provident fund delays up to 511 days and ESIC up to 770 days; CARO dues outstanding beyond six months at two subsidiaries in FY2026; six adjudication/compounding matters with penalties paid of Rs 32.00 mn, Rs 8.00 mn and Rs 0.89 mn (Company) and Rs 28.29 mn and Rs 2.00 mn (Bigtec); Section 133A tax survey demands of Rs 234.17 mn on allegedly bogus expense claims; a Form FC-GPR/FC-TRS filing for 36,700 / 9,175 Equity Shares still pending.

Rs 1,055.35 mn R&D facility (total project cost Rs 1,251.21 mn per the Koncepo project report; handover March 2028) and Rs 722.81 mn plant and machinery (total Rs 808.05 mn), Nil deployed as on July 15, 2026; only one of 18 machinery items ordered (Caliber LIMS Rs 11.50 mn); imports Rs 419.69 mn / 51.94%; no appraisal by any bank or independent agency; the R&D object is stated not to add manufacturing capacity or immediate cash flow.

red_flags: Disclaimer of opinion on internal financial controls in the FY2024 consolidated audit report - the auditor states the Holding Company had not established internal financial controls and was unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to form an opinion.

Income tax surveys under Section 133A at the Company and Bigtec for AY 2020-21 to AY 2023-24 on the stated ground that certain transactions classified as expenses in the books are bogus in nature, with demands of Rs 234.17 mn raised for AY 2020-21 to AY 2024-25.
Provident fund remittances delayed up to 511 days and ESIC up to 770 days across FY24-FY26, with statutory dues outstanding beyond six months at two subsidiaries as recently as FY2026.

Three disclosed fraud matters - Rs 199.00 mn of earnest money deposits misappropriated at Prognosys Medical (fully provided FY2024), Rs 6.09 mn by a Bigtec employee against fake and inflated purchase orders of Rs 7.66 mn, and Rs 4.43 mn by two external parties - with an Enforcement Directorate summons dated March 7, 2023 to a Prognosys Medical director in the related fake-tender matter.

Six-row table of past non-compliance under the Companies Act (Sections 135, 137(1), 117(1), 42(6) for the Company; Sections 135 and 185 for Bigtec) settled through adjudication and compounding with penalties paid in FY2025 and FY2026, i.e. in the run-up to the Offer.

Form 1 and Form 18 for the Company's incorporation and Form 32 for the initial appointment of Sriram Natarajan as Executive Director on October 20, 2000 are untraceable in the Company's records and on the MCA Portal; disclosure rests on the original Articles of Association and the minutes of the first Board meeting.

Audit-trail (edit log) facility absent or not enabled in certain accounting software in FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024, including at database level and for privileged/administrative access, and management cannot determine whether third-party-maintained software keeps daily backups on servers located in India.

Single-customer dependence of 56.52% of finished-goods revenue with no firm commitment agreement, in a tender-driven channel where the RHP itself flags that governments 'may cap the selling prices of our products below economic levels, or impose procurement ceilings'.
strengths_observed: Installed-base consumables model is now the bulk of the mix: test kits were Rs 10,348.20 mn / 73.98% of finished-goods revenue in FY26 (Rs 7,309.58 mn / 74.31% FY25; Rs 5,525.45 mn / 67.78% FY24) on a closed Truenat system that works exclusively with the Company's own kits; kit units sold rose 8.80 mn to 12.24 mn to 17.56 mn across FY24-FY26, with over 12,500 devices sold in over 90 countries till March 31, 2026.

Revenue from operations rose 41.68% from Rs 10,204.18 mn (FY25) to Rs 14,456.87 mn (FY26), against Rs 8,365.61 mn in FY24; EBITDA Rs 32,824.3 lakhs at a 22.56% margin and restated PAT Rs 1,641.40 mn at an 11.28% margin; RoCE 17.55% and ROE 15.59% in FY26.

Regulatory and IP position is documented rather than asserted: WHO endorsement of the Truenat TB chip as one of only two rapid molecular tests globally endorsed for initial TB diagnosis and rifampicin resistance (Source: 1Lattice Report); first Indian company to receive the Class C IVDR (EU 2017/746) Technical Documentation Assessment Certificate for Truenat CT/NG (2025); 16 patents, 29 trademarks, 11 designs and 3 copyrights in India and 191 patents in foreign jurisdictions; 43 assays across 30 diseases as of March 31, 2026.

Balance sheet carries cash of Rs 35,553.0 lakhs against total debt of Rs 41,263.8 lakhs on net worth of Rs 114,467.6 lakhs at March 31, 2026, and none of the Promoters' Equity Shares are pledged or otherwise encumbered as on the date of the RHP (shareholding pattern reports Nil for both Promoter and Public categories).

Working capital days improved to 166 (FY26) from 173 (FY25) and 187 (FY24), and the average credit cycle shortened to 86 days in FY26 from 125 days in FY25, even as absolute working capital rose to Rs 8,274.83 mn from Rs 4,881.67 mn.

Volume headroom exists on the current asset base without the proposed capex: FY26 capacity utilisation was 58.25% on 39,000,000 kit units of installed capacity and 42.30% on 5,400 devices; the Objects capex is directed at automation, not at adding kit lines.

R&D is funded and staffed at scale for the size of the business: Rs 874.56 mn spent in FY26 (6.05% of revenue from operations), against Rs 685.69 mn (6.72%) and Rs 597.77 mn (7.15%); R&D headcount at Bigtec rose 69 (March 31, 2024) to 114 (2025) to 153 (2026), and a further 34 assays for 22 diseases are stated as intended.

The Fresh Issue of Rs 2,000.00 mn is entirely capital expenditure and general corporate purposes - R&D facility and Centre of Excellence Rs 1,055.35 mn, plant and machinery for Goa Unit I, Goa Unit II and Visakhapatnam Rs 722.81 mn, GCP [dot] - with no debt-repayment or working-capital object, and the Bengaluru project land (43,490 sq ft) is Company-owned under a sale deed dated August 7, 2023, free from encumbrances.
